answers.note: Let's do all three, but it doesn't have to be (likely shouldn't be) the same block. When a guest name is clicked in the lightbox or guest room with the intention of learning more about that user/profile, making this screen open into a block-heavy view feels far less social, more administrative. Block should be a minor, more sublte action when opening a user preview. However, if 'block' is specifically clicked, that could funnel all into one screen.

Nice use reusing an existing lock screen to lock out blocked users, without the 'blocked' experience feeling distinct so guests won't be able to immediately discern they were blocked. Sneaky block, I like it.

I like the confirmation, with default toggled off. I'd expect the more likely case here is giving someone a second chance, but keeping their original media that led to the blocking as removed. However, a secondary case is accidentally blocking someone, where this offers an easy reversion to get their media back in.

I honestly can't think of many (if any) cases where a host would want everyone uploading into a shared album together, but keeping the guest uploaders secret. I think we should just make the guest list always on, so a host doesn't have to turn it on or learn special handling. If I have to upload to become a guest, and don't want to be listed as a guest, I simply shouldn't upload in the first place. This is a much easier mental model - we only want to add configs where the potential friction offers real benefit/value. This doesn't seem to. Always on for everyone.

Rather than make a selection here, I genuinely believe our event settings are some of our ugliest, most unintuitive UI despite being some of the most critical to handling events. Would prefer a dedicated exploration into revamping how settings are designed from the ground up. Should be made as streamlined as possible - nesting, disabled features, pro locks, groups, UI design, everything. This also leads me to a side point that I'd also like to shift a few more pro features on free, so the free plan feels very close to the same pro experience, minus a few core blockers that more clearly define what a pro upgrade includes (videos, more storage, unlimited events, no reel watermarks) rather than the less important stuff (reel clip time, event gating, etc). Then, if I'm a free user, I clearly know I love this app and want those few things on pro that unlock everything. The flip side of this is that free should become much more restrictive on storage (like 100mb) so while they get the full experience, it can't really be used for much more than a very small event without upgrading. That seems fair.

After thinking about it a bit, I feel like when a host closes an album, there are no cases where that closure should be differentiated by new guests that can't access beyond 'Closed'? Maybe a private version so previous guests of an event can see the host made it private versus a closed album (gated access), but does this selection feel like a pretty good universal answer? Feel like the design could be polished though, if this'll be a high-traffic screen.
Let's do this as the primary, but also add the 'use a different email' below as a secondary action. This handles both the "hey {host}, could you let me in" and "oops wrong email" situations.
